q-4031.name: Question 1
q-4031.worked_solution:
We can combine the two $\sqrt{3}$ terms together, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}10\sqrt{3}-7\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{2} & = \\ (10-7)\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{2} & = \\ 3\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-134546.name: Question 3
q-134546.worked_solution:
First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{500} & =\sqrt{100\cdot 5}=\sqrt{100}\cdot \sqrt{5}=10\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{500}+4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{5} & = \\ 10\sqrt{5}+4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt{5}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}10\sqrt{5}+4\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{5} & = \\ (10\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{5})+4\sqrt{10} & = \\ (10-2)\sqrt{5}+4\sqrt{10} & = \\ 8\sqrt{5}+4\sqrt{10} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-134546.html:
Question 3
?

Simplify 500+410−25.

a
85+410
b
125
c
1410−25
d
105+210
e
1610
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

500=100⋅5=100⋅5=105

As a result,

500+410−25=105+410−25

Now, we can combine the two 5 terms together:

105+410−25=(105−25)+410=(10−2)5+410=85+410

q-134543.name: Question 4
q-134543.worked_solution:
First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{125} & =\sqrt{25\cdot 5}=\sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{5}=5\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{125}-2\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{5} & = \\ 5\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt{5}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{5} & = \\ (5\sqrt{5}+3\sqrt{5})-2\sqrt{3} & = \\ (5+3)\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{3} & = \\ 8\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{3} & \end{aligned}

Question 4
?

Simplify 125−23+35.

a
85−23
b
285−23
c
55+3
d
65
e
63
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

125=25⋅5=25⋅5=55

As a result,

125−23+35=55−23+35

Now, we can combine the two 5 terms together:

55−23+35=(55+35)−23=(5+3)5−23=85−23

q-134567.name: Question 5
q-134567.worked_solution:
First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{162} & =\sqrt[3]{27\cdot 6}=\sqrt[3]{27}\cdot \sqrt[3]{6}=3\sqrt[3]{6} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{7}+5\sqrt[3]{162}-\sqrt[3]{6} & = \\ \sqrt{7}+5(3\sqrt[3]{6})-\sqrt[3]{6}= \\ \sqrt{7}+15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}. & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt[3]{6}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{7}+15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}= \\ \sqrt{7}+(15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}) & = \\ \sqrt{7}+(15-1)\sqrt[3]{6} & = \\ \sqrt{7}+14\sqrt[3]{6} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-134564.name: Question 6
q-134564.worked_solution:
First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{500} & =\sqrt[3]{125\cdot 4}=\sqrt[3]{125}\cdot \sqrt[3]{4}=5\sqrt[3]{4} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sqrt[3]{500}+\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3} & = \\ 4(5\sqrt[3]{4})+\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3} & = \\ 20\sqrt[3]{4}+\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt[3]{4}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}20\sqrt[3]{4}+\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3} & = \\ (20\sqrt[3]{4}+\sqrt[3]{4})-\sqrt{3} & = \\ (20+1)\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3} & = \\ 21\sqrt[3]{4}-\sqrt{3} & \end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:
